recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not revert to the 2018 reported element name or informationSource cardinality; those differences reflect later decisions. Revisit only if later unresolved work such as FHIR-49863 reaches Applied/Published or Pharmacy reopens the reporting semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-19313 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for STU3 asking MedicationRequest to add one element indicating a reported request and another informationSource element, plus guidance on MedicationRequest versus MedicationStatement.
initial_application: Jira records application as merge commit 65133c5c9a9c6b94e85467b69529239812f98374. Implementation commit e1b82bc5a61a35b623c05f0ac408111209e5c0bb added MedicationRequest.reported, MedicationRequest.informationSource, and scope/boundary narrative for non-authoritative reported medication orders.
additional_context: FHIR-17169 redirected the workflow-level reported intent request into MedicationRequest-specific elements, and FHIR-15105 records the MedicationStatement boundary context. Later Pharmacy decisions changed the literal current shape: reporting is now MedicationRequest.isRecordOfRequest, informationSource has later cardinality/target/wording updates, and related reconcile commits for FHIR-19517, FHIR-19640, FHIR-34195, FHIR-47855, and FHIR-28575 are already on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source edit was made because active build inputs already define MedicationRequest.informationSource, MedicationRequest.isRecordOfRequest, optional requester and recorder support, narrative guidance, and a patient-reported prescription example.
